q: How do I write hello world in Omega?
alt: Show me a minimal Omega program
What does the smallest .om program look like?
a:
Drake's minimal program is a `text` plus `fn main`:

```
text msg "hello from seeded Omega\n"
fn main to int
w = write 1 msg 0 len msg
if ne w long len msg
ret 1
end
ret 0
end
```

Compile it with the pinned compiler (`omc < hello.om > hello`), check the compile status is 0, then `chmod +x hello && ./hello`.

q: How do I compile and run an Omega program?
alt: What is the command to build a .om file?
How do I use omc?
a: `omc` reads the unit on stdin and writes a static AArch64 Linux ELF on stdout: `"$OMC" < prog.om > prog 2> prog.err`. Print `$?` and the stderr. Only if the status is 0 do you `chmod +x prog` and run it. Drake checks the sha256 of `seed/out/omc` against the pin before every compile.

q: What does the exit status of an Omega program mean?
alt: Why did my Omega program exit 44?
What does exit code 104 mean in Omega?
a: The status is `main`'s value modulo 256 (so `ret 300` exits 44). A runtime trap exits 100 plus the trap code: 101 signed overflow, 102 divide by zero, 103 bounds, 104 loop past its bound, 105 conversion that does not fit, 106 stack, 107 shift amount. Keep your own codes below 100 so they never look like traps.

q: Why is my write line refused?
alt: omc says error 16 on my write call
Can I call write without using its result?
a: `write` returns a `long`: bytes written or minus the Linux errno. A value cannot stand alone as a statement. Bind it and check it: `w = write 1 msg 0 len msg`. At the pinned compiler the bare `write` line is error 16; a bare call to your own value-returning function is error 7.

q: Does Omega have implicit type conversions?
alt: Why does omc refuse adding a uint and a long?
What is error 7 in Omega?
a: No. Drake's rule (decision 20) is that both inputs of an operation, a value and its target name, and an argument and its parameter must have the same type, or the line is error 7. Write the conversion yourself: `y = add ulong x 1` instead of `y = add x long 1`.

q: What is error 11 in Omega?
alt: Why is x = 5 refused?
Why can't I write add 2 3?
a: Error 11 is an ambiguous bare number: nothing gives it a type. `x = 5` for a new name and `add 2 3` both have it. Type the number: `x = uint 5`. A bare number is fine where the place types it, like `add a 4` or `ret 0`.

q: How do I write arithmetic in Omega without operators like +?
alt: Does Omega have infix operators?
How does prefix notation work in .om?
a: Every operation is a prefix word with a fixed number of inputs, so nesting needs no brackets: `add mul a a 4` is a*a + 4, `eq rem n 2 0` is n mod 2 == 0. `+` and `*` are not words; write `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `rem`.

q: Why did my Omega program exit 105?
alt: What is trap 5?
Does Omega truncate when converting to a smaller type?
a: Exit 105 is trap 5: a conversion whose value does not fit the new type, for example `uchar x` with x = 300. Omega never truncates silently. If you want the low byte, mask first: `uchar and x 255`.

q: How do I write a loop in Omega?
alt: What is the loop syntax in .om?
How do for and while work in Omega?
Show me a for loop in Omega
a:
Two shapes, each closed by `end`:

```
while ne b 0 bound 64
t = rem a b
a = b
b = t
end

for i ulong 10
s = add s i
end
```

`while` rechecks its condition every pass and runs at most N times (`bound N`, 1..999999). `for i T K` runs i = 0..K-1. `break` and `continue` work inside either.

q: What does bound mean in an Omega while loop?
alt: Why do Omega loops need a bound?
What happens without bound?
a: `bound N` promises the body runs at most N times. One more pass traps 4 and the program exits 104. Without `bound` the limit is 1000000. Drake chose this so no loop can run forever; you pick N from a proof written in a `note`, for example "a ulong has at most 20 digits".

q: Why did my Omega program exit 104?
alt: What is trap 4?
My loop stopped with 104
a: Exit 104 is trap 4: a loop made one pass more than its bound (or than the default 1000000). Re-check the termination argument behind your `bound`; the trap means the proof did not hold for this input.

q: How do I write a do-while or break out of a loop in Omega?
alt: Does Omega have break and continue?
How do I exit a loop early?
a: Use `while true bound N` and end the body with `if <done>` / `break` / `end`. `break` leaves the innermost loop; `continue` goes to its next pass (in a while, the condition and bound count run again). Outside a loop both are error 9.

q: Why is bound 1000000 refused?
alt: What is error 8 on a while line?
a: A written bound must be 1..999999; outside that it is error 8 (number out of range). If you really need a million passes, leave `bound` off (the default limit is 1000000) or split the work into nested loops with their own proofs.

q: How do I read stdin in Omega?
alt: How do I write a read loop in .om?
How do I read a whole file in Omega?
a:
Loop on `read 0 buf 0 len buf` until it returns 0, add each partial count, and stop with a distinct status if it is negative:

```
k = read 0 buf 0 len buf
if lt k 0
ret int neg k
end
```

Cap the total so the loop bound is a proof. Drake's full example is the `wc.om` in this lesson.

q: What does a negative result from read or write mean in Omega?
alt: Why did read return -9?
How do Omega host words report errors?
a: Every host word returns a `long`: a count (possibly partial), 0 at end of input for `read`, or minus the Linux errno. -9 is EBADF (bad descriptor). Never treat a negative result as end of input.

q: Why can't I pass a global array to a function in Omega?
alt: What is error 19?
How do functions share a buffer in Omega?
a: A global is never passed as an argument (error 19), and the arrays of one call must be distinct names. Name the global directly inside each function that uses it. Parameters carry scalars and local arrays with an exact type and length (`a view uchar 64`).

q: Does Omega have dynamic memory or malloc?
alt: How do I allocate an array at run time in Omega?
Is there free in Omega?
a: No heap and no `free` at this pin (decision 24). Use a `global` pool, or `new T N v` on the stack in a function's outermost block, with N a literal or an integer `const`. Heap allocation is an open 1.0 roadmap item (RM4).

q: How is the Omega compiler bootstrapped?
alt: What is the seed chain?
How do you build omc from nothing?
a: From 408 hand-written bytes: `seed0` (hex to bytes) builds `hex1` (labels), which builds `asm2` (named instructions), which builds `om4` (an Omegese translator), which builds `omc` from `seed/omc/omc.om`; omc then rebuilds itself twice and the copies must match. The only outside step is `load0.sh`, which uses POSIX `printf`. Run `sh seed/omega-from-seed.sh` in a disposable copy.

q: What does the compiler fixpoint prove?
alt: Does self-hosting prove the compiler is correct?
Is the seeded build diverse double compilation?
a: It proves consistency and provenance: omc reads its own source as om4 does, and the committed binary is exactly what this seed and source produce. It does not prove correctness (a changed source reaches its own fixpoint) and it is not diverse double compilation, because both parents come from one lineage. Correctness evidence comes from referees, fixtures and gates.

q: How do I verify the committed omc binary?
alt: How do I check the Omega compiler hash?
How do I rebuild omc myself?
a: Compare `sha256sum seed/out/omc` with `seed/out/omc.sha256` and the pin you were given, then copy `seed/` to a temp directory and run `sh seed/omega-from-seed.sh` there; it ends with `RC=0` and the fixpoint hash. In Drake's run it took well under a second and matched `befb8199...8a1d`.

q: Is any C used to build the Omega compiler?
alt: Does omc depend on gcc?
a: No C, gcc, as or ld writes a byte of the seed chain. The C compiler and GNU objdump appear only as referees that check answers (for example decoding every seed instruction). Other parts of the omega-mv repository still contain C awaiting migration; that is listed as unfinished work, not part of the compiler path.

q: Can Omega compile to WebAssembly?
alt: How do I get a .wasm from an .om file?
Does Omega have a wasm backend?
a:
Yes, for scalar functions. Put an `ir` line first so omc writes OSC IR v1, then run the Omega-written back end:

```sh
omc < seed/wasm/irwasm.om > irwasm && chmod +x irwasm
{ printf 'ir\n'; cat fns.om; } | omc > fns.ir
./irwasm < fns.ir > fns.wasm
```

The module has no imports or memory and exports each function by name.

q: What is IR mode in omc?
alt: What does the ir line do?
What can't IR mode compile?
a: A first line `ir` makes omc write OSC IR version 1 instead of AArch64 code. It covers scalar functions (up to 32, 6 parameters, calls to earlier functions, break). It refuses struct, global and text declarations (error 9) and floats, host words, continue, sizeof and offsetof (error 3), by name, never by skipping.

q: Does Omega support SPIR-V or GPUs through SPIR-V?
alt: Is there a SPIR-V backend for Omega?
Can Omega emit SPIR-V?
a: Not at the pinned commit. An open pull request, omega-mv #804, adds `seed/spirv/irspirv.om` (SPIR-V 1.0 OpenCL Kernel modules from the same IR), with author-reported CPU-only parity through PoCL. Until it merges and its gate is run, Drake labels it PROPOSED, and no GPU execution is claimed.

q: Why does a trap in wasm not show the Omega trap code?
alt: What happens when an Omega function traps in WebAssembly?
a: irwasm keeps every check (overflow, division by zero, shifts, conversions, loop guards) as a wasm trap, which surfaces as `WebAssembly.RuntimeError`. WebAssembly MVP has no way to carry Omega's numeric code, so compare with a native run (exit 100 + code) when you need it.

q: What is OM-2 in Omega?
alt: What does the om2 line do?
What is the OM-2 profile?
a: OM-2 is an opt-in profile of Omegese. If the first line that is not blank or a note is `om2` (or `om2 diag`, `om2 fmt`), the compiler adds checked layouts, fresh scratch, abstract sealed types, unroll, inline, rotates, hex literals, unsized views and `part` slices. Units without the line stay OM-1 with exactly their old meaning.

q: How do I describe a binary wire format in Omega?
alt: Does Omega have packed structs?
How do I set endianness of a field in Omega?
a:
Use an OM-2 `layout`:

```
om2
layout hdr 8
field magic uint at 0 big
field size ushort at 4 little
end
```

Then a parameter `c edit hdr` is an 8-byte uchar array and `put c magic v` stores with that width and byte order. Overlapping or out-of-range fields are error 29. Packed structs as such remain unsupported.

q: What are errors 27, 28 and 29 in Omega?
alt: What does obligation=init mean?
omc says error 29
a: They are OM-2 obligations: 27 `init` (a fresh element read before a definite write), 28 `ctor` (a `seal` outside its constructor, or an unknown `holds` predicate), 29 `layout` (a layout field past SIZE or sharing a byte). With `om2 diag`, stderr adds an `omc-diag` record with line, column, byte span and the bytes found.

q: What does the OM-2 guarantee matrix promise?
alt: Is OM-2 proven correct?
Is Omega constant time?
a: Per row, what the compiler proves, what it checks at run time, and what nothing establishes. For example, checked unsized-view indices and refused reads of unwritten fresh elements are SUPPORTED; the behaviour of arbitrary OM-2 programs is NOT ESTABLISHED; constant-time behaviour in general is NO CLAIM. Evidence is fixtures and mutants, not proofs.

q: What does omc error 12 mean and how do I fix it?
alt: Register pool exhausted in Omega
My Omega function is refused with error 12
a: Error 12: the function needs more than its 16 registers. Parameters, live names, each open loop's hidden counter and the current statement's temporaries all share the pool. Split the function into helpers with about 10 live names each, then check the split against a reference computation and a negative control, as Drake's `split.om` does.

q: What are the Omega compiler error codes?
alt: List the omc error numbers
What does omc: line N: error K mean?
a: omc exits with the code K. 3 unknown name, 4 line ends early, 5 extra words, 6 bad number, 7 type mismatch, 8 out of range, 9 word in a disallowed place, 10 duplicate name, 11 ambiguous number, 12 registers, 13 name over 8 characters, 14 capacity, 15 missing end, 16 syntax, 17 line after ret/break/trap, 18 missing ret, 19 global passed, 20 write to view/text, 21 constant index, 22 bad text, 23 size. OM-2 adds 27, 28, 29. `seed/omc/gate15.sh` pins one case per code.

q: Why is new refused with error 9?
alt: Can I create an array inside a loop in Omega?
What is error 9?
a: Error 9 is a valid word in a disallowed place. `new` is only allowed in a function's outermost block, so create the array once before the loop. Other error 9 cases: `break` or `continue` outside a loop, a seventh parameter, `free`, host words or globals in function mode.

q: Why is my variable name refused with error 13?
alt: How long can names be in Omega?
a: Every name except a function name is at most 8 characters (function names up to 63). `totalsize` (9) is error 13; use `total` or `tsize`.

q: What does error 16 mean in Omega?
alt: omc error 16 on my fn line
Syntax error in .om
a: Error 16 is syntax: a word the parser cannot use in that place. Common causes are C-style signatures (`fn main(x int)`), array parameters without a length (`a view uchar` instead of `a view uchar 4`), and a variable used as an array length in `new`.

q: Omega doesn't have a feature I need. What do I do?
alt: How do I add a new word to Omega?
Can I extend the Omega language?
a: Drake's rule: make that feature, in Omega. Write a concrete proposal (the need, the word, its types and result, the refusal codes, the gate fixture, the guide row), then implement it in `seed/omc/omc.om` with a fixture that can fail, update OMEGESE, audit the corpus for the newly reserved spelling, and rebuild the compiler fixpoint. Never fill the gap with a C or Python helper and call it Omega.

q: What did adding the random word to Omega involve?
alt: Show me a real example of a word added to omc
How was getrandom added to Omega?
a: One commit (3fba1c43): keyword id 135 and the `hrand` lowering in `omc.om` (slice check, then Linux syscall 278), a row in OMEGESE, the fixture `seed/host/tests/random.om` wired into `seed/host/gate.sh`, rung R17 in `seed/README.md`, a benchmark-corpus audit (103 files, 0 differences), and the rebuilt `seed/out/omc` with its new hash.

q: How do I generate random bytes in Omega?
alt: Is there a random function in Omega?
a: Use the host word `random A off n flags`: it fills a writable `uchar` slice from Linux getrandom and returns the bytes written or minus errno. `flags` is an `int` (0 blocks until ready). A text or view is error 20, a slice past the end traps 3.

q: Why can't I name a variable random or stat?
alt: Why is my variable name error 16?
a: Every keyword, including every host word (`random`, `stat`, `link`, `bind`, `send`, `fork` and more), is reserved, so using it as a name is refused (error 16 for `random = ulong 1` at the pinned compiler). Check the keyword table in `fn kw`, not memory.
